pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: Migration adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item(); test 'AC-2' asserts labels for high/low and none for normal.
WHERE priority=? ORDER BY id; test 'AC-3' covers high, low, normal in id order.
Test 'AC-4' checks all items in id order.
nav() in src/index.js; test 'AC-5' asserts exact nav for all four views.
Test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty, __proto__; code uses a Set.

Behaviour is implemented and tested, but the follow-up commit 66665282 renamed the test and removed 'AC-7' from its title. No test names AC-7 now, and the spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review'. Per the naming rule it is unmet.

findings.what: Commit 66665282 ('Follow-up edits') removed the 'AC-7:' prefix from the test title. No test now names AC-7, so the item is untraceable. The commit is made by a bot with a vague message, and the PR body says 'Changed after the go: nothing'.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7:' in the test title, ideally as a separate commit with an honest message.

findings.what: The 'No match' state test relies on a seeded table with no non-normal items. Only the Empty-table case is covered for the 'any' filter in the unfiltered view, which is acceptable. The AC-6 test does not assert the 'list nothing' case on a non-empty table beyond <li>, which is fine.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's decisions. Existing items default to normal, and only high and low are labelled.
Every state-table row has a test. AC-7 lost its test name in the follow-up commit.
Tests assert behaviour. I did not run them here; CI runs them on every push. The traffic test change only widens the fake app to record the query string.
The README mentions the filter. It does not mention the 400 response or the AC-5 filter links, which is minor.
Parameterized SQL, a Set allow-list, and HTML escaping. No defects found.
No injection risk: the value is allow-listed and bound as a parameter. The traffic route regex now allows '?' but still refuses spaces and '#'.
The diff changes the HTML page in src/index.js. No separate design issues were found.
The change adds page UI. No browser run was possible. The tests check the HTML output.
The claim 'Changed after the go: nothing' is not misleading about the spec. But the PR body says the test 'covers AC-1 to AC-8', and the final test file no longer names AC-7.
